provenance: patch 0x14: toolchain-diff CL 4.2 canonicalizes r/r cmp operand order (emits cmp esi,eax); FA spells cmp eax,esi
notes: fastcall char __fastcall w32G_87020_v4(int s, int e): int now=TIMESystemTime(); ec=e-s; if(ec==-1) goto exit1; for(;;){ if(now==s) return 0; s++; ec=e-s; if(ec!=-1) continue; break; } exit1: return 1 — v1/v2 let CL hoist an exit block BEFORE the loop body (jne-body / exit / body) with CL's inverted polarity; goto-exit1 + for(;;) + continue makes CL emit FA's layout (je exit, body, je exit-tail after loop, jne back-edge to the now-check). Declaring the call result ('int now = TIMESystemTime();' first) keeps now in eax. The single residual byte is the r/r cmp operand order: CL canonicalizes == regardless of spelling (v4 proved s==now same as now==s) → 2-byte patch 0x14 (3b f0 → 3b c6). The call rides CL's own stdcall ext _TIMESystemTime@0 (no map).

notes: __declspec(naked) void __stdcall w32G_95b40_v5(int l, int r, int y) with the chunk transcribed as inline __asm. Plain-C v1-v3 all fail on the wave-19/25 a1-first wall: CL /O2 uses a1 moffs for ALL four clip loads (eax every time) with r in ecx, while FA uses a1 for clipTop/clipBottom/clipLeft but 8b 0d for clipRight (ecx) and keeps r in eax — a byte patch can't fix it because CL's own obj reloc sits at the a1 imm site. Inline asm makes the register plan explicit: mov ecx, clipRight; mov eax, [esp+0Ch]. Also compares must spell the GLOBAL first (cmp eax, / cmp ecx,eax); value-first spelling (cmp edx,eax) emits the flipped operand order (v4 fail at 0x21/0x31). Single shared exit: jg/jl/jl all target the pop esi that FOLLOWS the call (pop esi / ret 0Ch after call G_UHline). tail = FA census pad 00 + 8d 49 00 + 8d a4 24 00 00 00 00. Externs _clipTop/_clipBottom/_clipLeft/_clipRight/_G_UHline@12 match the FA publics directly — no maps needed beyond the def rename.
